claim_text: Across three expanding rolling origins (1250, 1310, 1370; horizon=14), SARIMA(1,1,1)(1,0,1,7) (mean MAE 6.14, std 1.03, sMAPE 6.70%) and additive ETS (mean MAE 6.17, std 1.17, sMAPE 6.74%) outperform lag-7 seasonal-naive (mean MAE 7.29, std 1.36, sMAPE 7.86%); SARIMA passes the predeclared 5% development gate for TDo1.
protocol: 3 expanding rolling origins (1250,1310,1370), 14-day horizon, 9 fold rows
decision_bound: SARIMA frozen as candidate for TDo1 interval release; ETS/seasonal_naive retained as fallback
safety_or_fallback_rule: Fallback to additive ETS or seasonal_naive if SARIMA exceeds 5% MAE margin or fails convergence
limitation: Origin 1370 failure period (SARIMA MAE 7.21 vs naive 6.93); Ljung-Box p>0.51 does not prove independence; stockout censoring unmodeled

claim_text: Trained explicitly for 1,750 episodes across base seeds (11,23,37,51,71), the frozen (9,2,3) tabular Q-table cuts mean cost by 51.2% vs random (42.78 vs 87.75) and reaches 98.50% fill rate on 5 disjoint development seeds (100011..100071), though it slightly trails the transparent reorder heuristic (42.48 cost, 98.83% fill).
protocol: 1750 training episodes (seeds 11,23,37,51,71), evaluated on 5 disjoint seeds (100011..100071), 40 steps
uncertainty_or_repetitions: 5 disjoint 40-step episodes, cost std=5.04, fill std=0.007
decision_bound: Frozen q_table.npy (SHA256 61cce191...) submitted unchanged to TDo2 controlled evaluation; no superiority claimed over reorder
safety_or_fallback_rule: Fallback to transparent regime-aware reorder heuristic (targets 2/4) if controlled evaluation confirms higher cost or lower service
limitation: Sub-optimal action at high-regime state (stock=2, regime=1) due to finite exploration noise; discrete 2-regime Markov assumption
